scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router2 RIP version
Mechanism: router0 and router1 run RIPv2; router2 was switched
  to RIPv1. The two versions use different packet formats and
  v2 peers drop v1 updates by default (and vice versa). router2
  is "sending" updates that router1 ignores. router2's own
  connected networks stay in its RIB; only advertised ones
  vanish elsewhere.
Localization: router2
Root cause: RIP version mismatch (router2 v1, neighbors v2)
Fix: `vtysh -c "router rip" -c "version 2"` on router2

agent.diagnosis_text:
- Affected component: RIP routing process/version interoperability.
- Mechanism: After the change, router2 is running RIP version 1 (broadcast, classful) while router1 runs RIP version 2 only (multicast, classless). Router1 therefore rejects router2’s RIP updates. As the timer expired, router1 poisoned the previously learned routes (metric 16), removed them from the FIB, and kept other RIPv2 routes intact.
- Localization: The failure is on router2’s FRR RIP process advertising out eth2 (20.20.0.2) toward router1’s eth3 (20.20.0.1). Evidence:
  • router2 config: “router rip … version 1” (show running-config).
  • router1 config: “router rip … version 2” (show running-config) and “send 2, receive 2” on all interfaces (show ip rip status).
  • router1 marks packets from 20.20.0.2 as bad: “Gateway 20.20.0.2 BadPackets 7” (show ip rip status).
  • router1 no longer installs 1.0.0.0/8 and 128.168.0.0/16 in the RIB (show ip route), and its RIP DB shows them at metric 16 (show ip rip), i.e., unreachable.
- Root cause: A configuration change set router2’s RIP to version 1, creating a version mismatch with router1’s RIP version 2-only configuration.
- Corrective fix: Align RIP versions. Recommended: on router2, switch to RIP version 2 so it sends/receives v2 on all interfaces:
  router rip
    version 2
Alternatively, allow router1 to receive v1 (not preferred). After aligning versions, 1.0.0.0/8 and 128.168.0.0/16 will be accepted again and reappear in router1’s routing table. No filters/passive-interfaces are blocking updates (both show none configured).

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly localizes the failure to router2 (its RIP process on eth2/20.20.0.2) matching the required device identification.
The agent explicitly diagnoses a RIP version mismatch (router2 running RIPv1 while router1 runs RIPv2), matching the required component identification.
Recommends changing router2 to RIP version 2 (aligning versions), which matches the expected remediation.

The investigation log clearly shows router2 running RIP version 1 and router0 running version 2; the agent’s observations and RIP/routing outputs (though truncated) support the conclusion that a RIP version mismatch caused router1 to stop accepting routes from router2. The chain of inference (v1 vs v2 incompatibility → rejected updates → routes poisoned/removed) is logical and the essential checks were performed.
